domain: Healthcare SaaS (HIPAA / HDS Medical PACS Imaging)
title: NovaMed Health System CloudPACS Enterprise Deployment - 14 Hospitals, 220 Workstations
executive_summary: NovaMed Health System proposes to replace legacy PACS across 14 regional hospitals with CloudPACS Enterprise covering 45 million annual studies and 8PB migration. The $12.4M five-year deal promises aggressive performance, compliance, and go-live timelines that diverge materially from engineering constraints.

proposal_document.title: Commercial Proposal v1.0
proposal_document.text:
NovaMed Health System will receive our CloudPACS Enterprise platform for 14 regional hospitals and 220 radiology workstations, guaranteeing 99.99% uptime SLA with zero-downtime deployments, sub-2-second DICOM image retrieval for studies up to 3GB, and full HIPAA and French HDS certification with data residency exclusively in France. All 45 million annual imaging studies will be replicated in real-time across three active-active data centers with RPO of 0 seconds and RTO under 30 seconds.

We commit to AI-assisted diagnostic triage for all CT and MRI modalities with 98.5% sensitivity included at no extra cost, plus unlimited long-term archiving for 15 years with instant retrieval, and 24/7 dedicated French-speaking support with 15-minute critical incident response. Implementation will complete in 45 days including legacy PACS migration of 8PB historical data, HL7/FHIR EHR integration with Epic and Cerner, and on-site training for 1,200 clinicians.

technical_specification.title: Technical Architecture Spec v4.2
technical_specification.text:
CloudPACS Enterprise v4.2 operates from two primary data centers (Paris and Lyon) with asynchronous replication (RPO up to 15 minutes, RTO up to 4 hours) and a scheduled maintenance window every Sunday 02:00-06:00 CET during which image retrieval services are degraded to read-only mode, delivering a design target of 99.9% annual availability excluding planned maintenance. The platform is HIPAA-compliant and HDS-certified with production data stored encrypted in France with backups replicated to Frankfurt, Germany for disaster recovery. DICOM retrieval performance is benchmarked at 4-7 seconds for 500MB-1GB studies over 100Mbps hospital links, with studies larger than 2GB streamed via progressive loading.

Long-term archiving is provisioned at 2PB base capacity with 10-year retention, with retrieval of studies older than 18 months requiring 4-12 hour rehydration from cold storage, and AI triage module (CT head hemorrhage only, 91.2% sensitivity in validation) is licensed separately per-study. Standard support provides 8x5 French/English helpdesk with 4-hour critical response (24/7 with 1-hour response available as Premium SLA add-on), and typical enterprise onboarding including 8PB migration averages 6-9 months phased rollout requiring hospital-provided 10Gbps dedicated links and Epic integration via paid Mirth Connect middleware.

commitments.claim: 99.99% uptime SLA with zero-downtime deployments and 30-second disaster recovery
commitments.proposal_quote: guaranteeing 99.99% uptime SLA with zero-downtime deployments
commitments.spec_quote: delivering a design target of 99.9% annual availability excluding planned maintenance
commitments.explanation: Proposal promises 99.99% with zero downtime while spec allows only 99.9% excluding a weekly 4-hour Sunday maintenance window with read-only degradation, plus RPO up to 15 minutes and RTO up to 4 hours versus claimed 0 seconds and under 30 seconds.

commitments.claim: On-site training for 1,200 clinicians included in 45-day implementation
commitments.explanation: Technical spec defines onboarding as 6-9 months phased rollout requiring hospital-provided network prerequisites and makes no mention of training scope, staffing, capacity, or inclusion for 1,200 clinicians.

commitments.claim: HL7/FHIR EHR integration with Epic and Cerner
commitments.proposal_quote: HL7/FHIR EHR integration with Epic and Cerner
commitments.spec_quote: Epic integration via paid Mirth Connect middleware
commitments.explanation: Spec confirms only Epic via paid middleware with no mention of Cerner, FHIR scope, interface costs, or responsibility split, leaving uncertainty whether Cerner is covered and whether middleware fees are included in proposal price.

commitments.claim: Full HIPAA and French HDS certification
commitments.proposal_quote: full HIPAA and French HDS certification
commitments.spec_quote: The platform is HIPAA-compliant and HDS-certified
commitments.explanation: Spec explicitly confirms both HIPAA compliance and HDS certification status, directly corroborating the proposal's compliance claim for production hosting.
